title: A New Method For Manipulating Circuits, Application To Quantum Adders
abstract: We use a new technique for manipulating controlled quantum circuits to convert between two distinct types of quantum adders, one based on the Quantum Fourier Transform and the other based on the Ripple-Carry technique from classical reversible logic. This conversion takes the form of an explicit gate-level transpilation. We also present a new quantum adder with a natural interpretation as a kind of Carry-Lookahead adder that uses no ancillas.
summary: This paper rigorously proves the equivalence between three major quantum adder designs—QFT-based, Carry-Lookahead, and Ripple-Carry—by performing explicit, gate-level circuit transpilation. The work introduces a novel, ancilla-free CL-Adder and demonstrates that these fundamentally different approaches compute the same function using equivalent quantum circuits.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish the equivalence between three distinct quantum adder circuits: one based on the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT), one based on the classical Ripple-Carry (RC) logic, and a novel Carry-Lookahead (CL) adder.
main_result: The authors prove that the QFT-Adder, the CL-Adder, and the RC-Adder are all equivalent through explicit, gate-level transpilation, culminating in an ancilla-free CL-Adder implementation.
method: The core method involves using hierarchical quantum circuits and algebraic manipulation, applying inductive proofs and known quantum circuit identities to transform one adder structure into another.
model_or_system: The system modeled is quantum addition implemented via quantum circuits. The circuits are compared across three architectures: QFT-based, CL-based, and RC-based, utilizing standard reversible gatesets like {X, CNOT, Toffoli}.
key_observables: Circuit depth, the number of required ancilla qubits (achieving ancilla-free operation is key), and the explicit gate-level transformation between the three adder forms.
important_parameters: The bit length ($n$) of the numbers being added, and the specific gate sets used for representation.
main_assumptions: The equivalence proofs rely heavily on specific commutation and anti-commutation relations between quantum gates and the assumption that the CL-Adder structure can be successfully mapped onto the QFT-Adder structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the graphical language for hierarchical circuits, the recursive definitions of the QFT-Adder and CL-Adder, and detailed steps showing the transpilation process, such as pushing the CL-Adder prefix through the stages of the RC-Adder.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the QFT-Adder and the RC-Adder, then presenting the novel CL-Adder. It then proves the equivalence $	ext{QFT-Adder} \leftrightarrow 	ext{CL-Adder}$ via transpilation, followed by proving $	ext{CL-Adder} \leftrightarrow 	ext{RC-Adder}$ through a final series of gate manipulations and inductive steps.
why_interesting: While the topic is quantum computation, the rigorous, gate-level comparison of different adder architectures (QFT vs. Carry-Lookahead vs. Ripple-Carry) provides deep insights into the structural overhead and computational equivalence of fundamental quantum arithmetic operations.
